box_cover.coverage: Each initial closed rectangle is recursively bisected into two closed children; every final child is either certified nonzero or contained in the frozen disk.
box_cover.criterion: At box centre m, |P_N(m)| > TAIL0_UP + M1_UP*((sigma width+t width)/2).

domain_reduction.direct_box_domain: All eight closed products [0.73,0.75] x phase interval
domain_reduction.included_boundaries: The products and all leaf boxes are closed; hence sigma=0.73 and every retained ordinate endpoint are included. The phase cover also covers the possible top boundary t=8596696.
domain_reduction.phase_cover: Every remaining zero with 0.73<=Re(s)<sigma_F and 0<t<=8596696 has t in one of the eight closed input intervals.
domain_reduction.source_theorem: Mantovanelli Theorem 1.1: no zeros for Re(s)>=sigma_F and sigma_F<0.75

method_notes: Arb comparisons are strict interval comparisons; an assertion succeeds only when the displayed inequality is certified.
The value and derivative tails use F_n>=phi^(n-2), F_n<=phi^(n-1), and exact geometric-series sums; both Fibonacci inequalities follow by induction from phi^2=phi+1.
The nonzero box criterion follows by integrating Z_F' along the line segment from the box centre and using the uniform derivative bound on Re(s)>=0.73.
Exactly one zero counted with multiplicity implies existence, uniqueness as a distinct zero, and simplicity.

rouche_disk.argument: The linear function has one zero inside the disk. On the circle its modulus lower bound exceeds the value-tail + derivative-tail*r + M2*r^2/2 bound for Z_F minus the linear function, so Rouche gives exactly one zero counted with multiplicity and none on the circle.
